steps.observation: Work on this for 30 seconds; do not stop early. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Rain lashed against the rough-hewn walls of Seaward Point Lighthouse, the gusts rattling its ancient windows like impatient ghosts. Within, Thomas Hale, the third-generation keeper, stood vigil beside the great Fresnel lens. Each hour he wound the brass mechanism, coaxing the light to pulse across the stormy sea.

It had been a lonely year since his wife, Margaret, had passed, and every night Thomas spoke quietly to the phantom echo of her laughter, as if she still paced the spiraling stairs beside him. Tonight’s gale was the fiercest yet: breakers thundered against the craggy reef, and every sailor in these waters relied on his beam.

Just before midnight, a shrill horn cut through the howling wind. At the base of the cliff, a fishing trawler floundered, its deck awash with foam. Thomas’s heart pounded. He grabbed the signal lamp, swinging its red-and-white beam in rhythmic arcs. The tempest snapped at his fingers, but he held fast, calling out Morse code: “Stay on course. Keep steady.”

As minutes stretched, a distant shape emerged through the rain—a battered ship’s silhouette slipping safely past the reef. When at last the trawler passed Seaward Point, its crew flashed grateful lamps back at him. Thomas exhaled, the weight in his chest lifting.

Later, drenched but triumphant, he climbed to the lantern room’s summit and whispered to the empty air, “Goodnight, Margaret.” The great light pulsed once more, carving hope through darkness—just as he always had.
